messages:
maya: quick check: the int4-v2 variant we shadowed against main-summ has a consistent dip on long-doc rouge-l, seen in the smoke run this morning. anyone else seeing this? :eyes:
lucas: saw that, yep. overall token cost down, latency good, but long-context f1/recall lower on the 8k+ bucket. short docs look fine.
tobias: do we have the eval slices? can you paste the CLI run?
maya: pasted below — ran the usual corpus slice for 8k+ windows:```./tools/eval_summary --model=redwood/int4-v2 --slice=long-docs --n=500 --metrics=rouge,f1,prec,latency```
lucas: run output (excerpt):
```
slice: long-docs (n=500)
model: redwood/main-ptv1  rouge-l: 0.412 latency(ms): 210
model: redwood/int4-v2      rouge-l: 0.378 latency(ms): 185
delta rouge-l: -0.034  p<0.01
average gen tokens: main 480 vs int4-v2 472
```

anika: delta is small but systematic. could be sampling/truncation or kv-cache precision. int4 often shrinks subtle token probabilities, which can change beam/argmax choices on long deps.
maya: good point. i also noticed more early-stops in decodes for int4-v2 (~5% vs 1%).
tobias: do we run with the same decoding params across variants? e.g. `max_new_tokens`, `eos_penalty`, `do_sample=false`? small mismatch there would amplify.
lucas: yes, same config — I double-checked the route config in rollout manifest. 
maya: hypothesis: quantized logits at long sequences drift and produce earlier eos token in some contexts. propose a two-step: 1) run deterministic beam (no sampling) with forced min length; 2) shadow with a prefix-preserve KV cache enabled and compare token-level diffs.
anika: agree. also add a token-level edit-distance slice and look at position of eos. a delta at token 420 vs 480 will highlight premature truncation.
eval-bot: queued eval: eval-id=eval-3865432116, tasks=[long-docs-token-diff,long-docs-minlen-beam], notify=@maya @lucas @tobias @anika
maya: thx eval-bot. lucas, can you export a mini set of 50 failing cases (int4 shorter than main) to /tmp/int4_short_samples.json? put short context + outputs.
lucas: done: /tmp/int4_short_samples.json (50 cases). sample looks like early eos in instruction-following sections. attaching one example inline:
```
ctx: "...policy recommendation: when migrating..."
main out (truncated): "We recommend a phased migration over 6 months with staging and canary... [continues]"
int4-v2 out: "We recommend a phased migration."  <-- stops early
```
tobias: nice. next diagnostic: run the same 50 with `force_decode_min_tokens=200` and see if content matches after that. if yes, it's truncation. if no, it's fidelity change.
anika: also test with small temperature change (0.0 vs 0.2) and top_k/top_p to see if quant noise interacts with stochasticity.
maya: timeline: can we get eval results and token diffs by EOD? if it's a truncation fix we can try a rollout knob: `min_decode_length` on the variant or a prefix-fallback to the float model for sequences > 4k.
lucas: running now, eval-id returns partial: long-docs-minlen-beam done at 3865432133, token-diff in progress.
eval-bot: eval-3865432116 result snippet: long-docs-minlen-beam -> passes (delta rouge-l ~ -0.005 when minlen forced), long-docs-token-diff -> queued.
maya: interesting — forcing minlen narrows the gap a lot. that points at premature eos.
tobias: if so, we can add a temporary rollout gate: auto-fallback when average eos-pos < 0.95 * expected_eos_pos on long-doc slice. simple circuit-breaker.
anika: agree. we should codify as: if relative eos-position < 0.9 and rouge-l delta < -0.02 on the long-doc slice -> auto-fallback to main-ptv1 for that route.
lucas: i'll add that as a canary rule in the manifest:```canary_rules:
  - slice: long-docs
    metric: eos_pos_ratio
    threshold: 0.9
    action: fallback-to=redwood/main-ptv1
```
maya: great. also, let's schedule a mini quant-retrain with calibration table for logits if this recurs. open follow-up ticket?
tobias: creating ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-4721 - "int4-v2 premature-eos calibration" assigned to lucas.
lucas: ack, will take.
maya: thanks all. next check after token-diff done — ping here once eval-bot posts final. :thumbsup:
